NOTES.text:
Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module two on nanomaterials and in this class we are going to talk about properties of nanomaterials, surface area dependent properties, electrical properties and optical properties.

Key details

  • Properties of nanomaterials are very different from that of the bulk materials.
  • We find that for bulk material the properties are independent of size whereas when we come to nanomaterials they change with size.
  • Then it is it has a particular colour that is called golden colour.
  • There is no change in the colour, it still continues to remain in that golden colour.
  • But that is not true when we come to the nanoparticle range.
  • Gold, when we get it into the nanoparticle range, we find that as we decrease the size, the colour of gold also.
  • That the optical properties are getting altered with the dimension of the particles.
  • Is what happens for all most of the properties of nanomaterials.
  • They change with size.
  • Whereas in nanomaterials, the material remains the same.
  • The structure composition remains the same, it's only the size which is changing, and that can alter the properties.
  • We know that many physical and chemical properties of a material are going to depend on surface properties, and when we come to nanomaterials, the surface area has enormously increased.
  • We have a bulk material over here, it is being broken down into smaller particles.
  • We know that the surface area has increased so much over here.
  • The surface area.
  • And we know that since in nanomaterials the surface atoms are much more than what the atoms at inside the bulk of the material and therefore.
  • All the properties are mostly dictated by the surface atoms.
  • And since we have such a large surface area, such a large number of surface atoms, therefore the properties which depend on surface area definitely get affected when you take.
  • the particle when take the material from bulk to nanocyte.
  • So properties like catalytic activity we know that whenever we use a catalyst we prefer to take it in the powder form because we want to increase the surface area and catalytic catalysis is a surface phenomena.
  • If we take it in nano range, nano particle range, the catalytic activity is going to increase enormously.
  • Are found to be catalytically very active for selective redox reactions.
  • Because there are a lot of surface atoms which are held much less tightly as compared to the bulk atoms.
  • For nanoparticles, it is found that electrical conductivity decreases as compared to the bulk material.
  • One important reason for that is spatial confinement.
  • We talked about spatial confinement also, and we understood that as we go into the nanoparticle range.

Example or application from the lecture

  • For example, if we have a block of gold.
  • Now even if you make it into smaller and smaller size, like for example, the block of gold which was say hundred grams, now we make it into a five gram piece, by breaking it into smaller pieces, we find that.
  • Let us look at the most important property of nanomaterials, the surface area.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

The energy levels become more and more discrete, and the band gap increases or the energy gap increases.

Key details

  • What are we talking about here?
  • Now when we have metals, we know that the valence band and the conductance band are overlapping and therefore the.
  • Electrons can easily move into the conduction band and we find that metals are good conductors.
  • Whereas in insulators the energy gap is very high and therefore they are not found to conduct electricity.
  • Whereas in semiconductors the band gap is less.
  • Energy gap is less now, and therefore, it is possible that if we give the right energy, the electrical conduction is possible.
  • You can see the same energy.
  • Semiconductor now the band gap has become more and obviously when the band gap is more than the conductivance properties are going to get altered.
  • you can see here this the band gap is so high, so obviously the conductance has become less and they can almost be acting like insulators.
  • Another important reason is due to surface scattering.
  • What is a mean free part for an electron?
  • the distance which the electrons move before they undergo some collusion.
  • We know that the electron has a mean prepared and there's no obstruction.
  • But when we have the same bulk material into the nanoparticle range, now we know that the nanoparticle has become has a very small dimension.
  • Changing its direction and therefore there is conservation of energy as well as momentum.
  • Whereas if it is inelastic scattering, then when the electron is scattered in randomly in all directions.
  • We find that the scattered electron now loses its velocity, and when the electron loses its velocity, it's understood that the.
  • Mobility is now less and therefore the electrical conductivity decreases.
  • Coming to the next property that is optical properties.
  • Nanomaterials show unique optical properties.
  • As I mentioned, the colour depends on the size of the particles.
  • In the bulk material, there is no change in colour even if you decrease the size.
  • But when you come into the nano range, it is found that as we change the size of the particles, there is a change in colour.
  • One is due to the surface plasmon resonance and the other is due to increase in band gap.
  • If you look at metals.
  • This is the picture of a metal.
  • What happens is the.
  • Electric field which is fluctuating, the electromagnetic radiation which is formed falling on the surface, it has an electric field.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let's understand what is the surface plasmon resonance.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

Because the lattice point is positive, these is an electron cloud which is getting formed, there is an attraction which is going to pull these electrons back.

Key details

  • Up in the in the system.
  • This collective oscillation of these electrons is what is known as the plasmon.
  • Collective oscillations of these electrons is what is known as plasma.
  • Then there is going to be resonance.
  • When resonance happens, we know that the radiation is going to be absorbed, and when radiation is absorbed in the visible light, then the material appears to be colored.
  • This is going to depend on the size, shape and nature of the metal.
  • Now it is not just the just this happens because there's an electron cloud and a positive metal side.
  • It is not the same for all the metals.
  • It is going to depend on the nature of the metal, it also depends on the size of the particle.
  • Why is it dependent on the size of the particles?
  • Because we know that the electric field there is a polarization.
  • This electric field is definitely going to depend on the size, not only on the size, it also depends on the shape.
  • Whether the particle is spherical or whether it's rod shaped or it's a platelet shape, then definitely the.
  • Electric field is going to be different each time, and therefore the plasma frequency is different.
  • And if the plasmon frequency is different, definitely the light absorbed is going to also be different.
  • Therefore, as the size of the particle changes, the color of the.
  • The nanoparticle also changes.
  • Another reason is the increase in the energy gap.
  • This is again what we have understood before as spatial confinement or quantum confinement.
  • We know that as we go into the nanoparticle range, when we go to smaller and smaller sizes, the energy levels become more discrete and the energy gap increases.
  • Now if energy gap increases, obviously the wavelength of the light absorbed is going to be different and therefore.
  • As we increase as the energy gap goes on increasing, then the energy required is going to be more, so the wavelength is going to be less.
  • And that is exactly the reason why we find that as the size of the nanoparticles becomes.
  • Smaller and smaller, we find a blue shift which happens in the in the particles.
  • Is decreasing the energy gap increase.
  • This we understood in when we were talking about spatial confinement and the wavelength of the light absorbed, as I mentioned just now, goes towards smaller values, and this is referred to as blue shift.
  • Suspensions of gold nanoparticles, as you can see here, as the size is increasing, or if we say as the size is decreasing, we find there is a change in color.
  • This is very characteristic of nanoparticles.
  • Nanoparticles gold spheres which have greater than 50 nanometers they absorb at a wavelength of 575 nanometers now gold spheres 10 to 20 nanometers absorb at 524 nanometers whereas 2 to 5 nanometers absorb at 517 nanometers what does it mean?
  • The wavelength has become less, that means the frequency is more, that means the energy gap is more.
  • As we decrease the size, we find that.
  • the energy gap is becoming more and more and the light now is now moving the wavelength is now moving more towards the violet so we call it as the blue shift.

Example or application from the lecture

  • So let us take the example of gold.

So in the next class we are going to talk about some more properties of nanomaterials like the mechanical properties, the thermal properties, and magnetic properties.
